event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: EXC’s February 2021 filing squarely acknowledges that COVID-19 is already depressing revenue, raising credit-loss expense, creating new direct operating costs and forcing emergency liquidity draws.  The risk is therefore not merely potential but current and quantified: management discloses a $170 million hit to Generation net income and a $75 million hit to the utilities for 2020 alone, alongside specific liquidity actions totalling more than $2 billion.  The disclosures span both operational disruption (work-force safety, remote-work, supply-chain constraints) and financial stress (lower demand, higher bad-debt, capital-market volatility).  While the company lists several mitigants—regulatory deferral, cost-savings, new credit facilities—these are presented as responses, not eliminations, of risk.  Because the pandemic began less than one year before the balance-sheet date, the Time-Decay principle allows high scores (7-10) where the text shows direct, recent, quantified impact; generic or heavily mitigated statements score lower.  The evidence set below captures every sentence that materially advances the disclosure of pandemic-related risk, with micro-scorecards that balance aggravating and mitigating elements and then sum to a final snippet score consistent with the 0-3-year window.

evidence_list.snippet: the ability of the Registrants to operate their respective generating and transmission and distribution assets, their ability to access capital markets, and the impacts on their results of operations due to the global outbreak (pandemic) of the 2019 novel coronavirus (COVID-19),

components.reason: Explicitly links operational capability, capital-market access and earnings to COVID-19.
Generic, forward-looking bullet with no quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies multiple enterprise-wide risk channels, but in generic terms and without figures, warranting a moderate score of 5.

evidence_list.snippet: The Registrants' results could be negatively affected by the impacts of COVID-19 (All Registrants).

components.reason: Head-line risk factor flagging negative earnings impact.
No specificity or quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: A formal risk-factor caption signals materiality but offers no details; low-mid score.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 is an evolving situation that could lead to extended disruption of economic activity in the Registrants’ respective markets.

components.reason: States broad macro-economic disruption possibility.
Future-oriented and unquantified.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes potential for prolonged disruption—important but still abstract—score 5.

evidence_list.snippet: COVID-19 could negatively affect the Registrants’ ability to operate their respective generating and transmission and distribution assets, their ability to access capital markets, and their results of operations.

components.reason: Enumerates concrete operational and financial risk vectors.
Contingent language (‘could’), no magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Lists specific channels of harm but remains hypothetical; moderate weight.

evidence_list.snippet: Unfavorable economic conditions due to COVID-19 have impacted the demand for electricity and natural gas at Generation and the Utility Registrants, which has resulted in a decrease in operating revenues.

components.reason: Declares a realised decrease in demand and revenue.
No dollar amount provided.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirmed impact on top-line makes this high-severity despite lack of figures.

evidence_list.snippet: At Generation, such measures resulted in an increase in credit loss expense.

components.reason: Direct accounting impact (higher bad-debt).
No quantification.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete income-statement effect raises risk but unquantified; score 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Generation and the Utility Registrants have also incurred direct costs related to COVID-19 consisting primarily of costs to acquire personal protective equipment, costs for cleaning supplies and services, and costs to hire healthcare professionals to monitor the health of their employees.

components.reason: Specifies new categories of operating expense attributable to COVID-19.
Lacks numerical magnitude.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Identifies tangible cost pressures, so above-average risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: The estimated impact to Generation’s and the Utility Registrants’ Net income is approximately $170 million and $75 million for the year ended December 31, 2020, respectively.

components.reason: Provides specific, quantified, already-incurred earnings hit.
Recent (same fiscal year) and material.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highly material, recent, quantified loss—near-maximum severity.

evidence_list.snippet: As a result of the disruptions in the commercial paper markets in March of 2020, Generation borrowed $1.5 billion on its revolving credit facility to refinance commercial paper, which Generation repaid on April 3, 2020.

components.reason: Shows liquidity stress triggered directly by pandemic market disruption.
Repayment indicates mitigation.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Liquidity strain evident but quickly resolved; risk tempered.

evidence_list.snippet: Generation also entered into two short-term loan agreements in March of 2020 for an aggregate of $500 million.

components.reason: Additional emergency borrowing underscores liquidity risk.
No statement of difficulty or ongoing exposure.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Reveals reliance on extra debt; moderate liquidity risk.

evidence_list.snippet: To offset the unfavorable impacts from COVID-19, the Registrants identified approximately $250 million in cost savings across Generation and the Utility Registrants in 2020.

components.reason: Quantified mitigation effort.
Demonstrates management response capacity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Material mitigation lowers net risk; negative score counter-balances other snippets.

evidence_list.snippet: The Registrants assessed long-lived assets, goodwill, and investments for recoverability and there were no material impairment charges recorded in 2020 as a result of COVID-19.

components.reason: States absence of impairments—strong mitigating evidence.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Affirmative mitigation reduces severity; small negative score.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which COVID-19 may impact the Registrants’ ability to operate their generating and transmission and distribution assets, the ability to access capital markets, and results of operations, including demand for electricity and natural gas, will depend on the spread and proliferation of COVID-19 around the world and future developments, which are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted at this time.

components.reason: Emphasises continuing uncertainty across multiple risk dimensions.
Lack of quantification keeps it below top tier.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Wide-ranging uncertainty elevates risk to mid-level.

evidence_list.snippet: Generation temporarily suspended interruption of service for all retail residential customers for non-payment and temporarily ceased new late payment fees for all retail customers from March to May of 2020.

components.reason: Shows direct operational concession impacting cash collection.
Temporary measure, already ended.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Cash-flow risk acknowledged but partly time-bounded.

evidence_list.snippet: Starting in March of 2020, the Utility Registrants also temporarily suspended customer disconnections for non-payment and temporarily ceased new late payment fees for all customers and restored service to customers upon request who were disconnected in the last twelve months.

components.reason: Utility-wide suspension magnifies credit-loss exposure.
Action framed as temporary mitigation for customers, not permanent harm.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Collectability risk, partly mitigated by temporariness.
